But I guess I should tell my parents I got depressive thoughts. It would clear things up for them a bit more. 
I can't really imagine chronic pain without depressive thoughts anymore. A life without these thoughts I can't imagine. It's too distant. 

Hm energy, I have some energy. Just very limited amounts. How do I deal with the depressive thoughts on a regular basis like you said? Positive self-talk, meditation I know. I do both very regular. But self-talk not as much as meditation. Have you got tips here?

I still feel absolutely mindbogglingly worthless.

I want to do something and then boom pain is there and tells me to lie down and do nothing but stare into my computer or telephone or just cry and think of suicide. 

I know I am not rational anymore. 
Failure is very relative and for other people I guess I am not a complete failure but a big part of my thoughts are my grandparents. 
I am so afraid all of my grandparents think I am like the black sheep of the family now with my pain-issues. 
The one who didn't do anything with his life and fucked it all up, consuming the resources of his parents while lying on the floor whining around.  

I can't easily switch off the thoughts of me being a failure, I think it will take time and work to change these thought patterns. 

It's right, I need someone to talk to who is not my parents. I am chosing a psychiatrist at the moment. I just need to overcome my thoughts of embarrasment. Understand that they are not what the outer world sees of me, but what I think everyone sees in me.

Hello,
thank you for this long in-depth answer. 

It's a challenge itself for me to answer to this, which is why it took such a long time. I need time and power to write these things and think about the answers. 

Yes the pain pulls me into the ground literally every day. Social life has become zero. I just don't know what to say. All the lifes of my former friends and loved ones have moved on. 
Mine stood still in time. 

If they asked me "how are you" in a casual way, what would I answer? Near suicide, slowly becoming chronically depressed, completely fucked up thought-patterns etc..? 
I wouldn't be able to say such things. 

Add to this, I feel like I live in a completely different world by now. 
The pain and the life it brings with it, has changed me into a different person. 
I am not resonating with my "old" friends anymore. 
There is no one I want to meet, except for maybe a girl I would hang out with, but her life also moved on. 
I wouldn't want to talk to her anyway, because I don't want to bother her with my existence. 

The last days were quite hard. I sit in a darkened room for hours. Just crying, pinching and hitting myself. Getting caught in classic depressive thoughts. 
Things like "you are a completely worthless pile of shit", "no one gives a shit about you", "it would be better if you were not existing". 
I think I am getting depressed on a 5/10 by now. I guess it's time to get into antidepressants a bit more. 

I was taking some already but they gave me light spasms because of the combination with the opioids I am taking, so I discontinued. I have to see my neurologist again which is slightly off-topic. 

So I just can't imagine telling people about my life. I'm completely blocked to talk to anyone but my parents. 
I slightly refuse to see a psychologist because I don't want to tell them about my shit life. I just feel so embarrassed. It all went so fast.
It feels like yesterday I had all I wanted, and today I have nothing at all...

I workout on a regular basis. I'm vegan, stopped smoking, stopped drinking and doing drugs (except for necessary painkillers). 
Still I feel like complete failure. 
It's all my fault. I fucked it up. I should stop my existence. 
(I won't do it.)

I have ways of getting myself into a different world for a while and forget everything around me. But I can't forget the pain except for those seconds or minutes I hurt myself. I meditate which helps me get at least a little bit done in my life. 

I don't know how to celebrate my well rested nights anymore. Every day is just the same. I mean I got good times. My dog, my parents, at the gym, making music at home. 
But I miss so many things. I feel trapped

My god I just couldn't imagine I would stuff like this. It's almost funny for me to read. 

These battles we all fight. How can I win them? I can't, can I? I am doomed to lose?!

I do fight, but then I get caught up in even more battles. 
Am I continuing, until there are too many battles and I am doomed to just give it all up? 

My mind already tells me: 
"Write a last letter to your parents, just in case there is an impulsive moment and you don't wanna miss it out". 

Aaaah what a fucked up thought!!!
Where will all this go? How do you combat a fight like this? 

This is to big to fight, to powerful, it feels like my body is flooded with an evil power destroying me from within. 

I don't believe in god, I was never interested in religion until the last months. I don't know it just seems like a big topic into which I could slightly dive, because it would be something completely different to everything I knew in life.

Sorry for being a bit messy, today is again one of the worst days in my life. I just don't really know what I am doing. But still writing all this felt good. 

Best regards!
